ओपनिंग वीकेंड में आयुष्मान खुराना और सारा अली खान की फिल्म उड़ता तीर का बॉक्स ऑफिस पर कमाल का जलवा 🎬✨

इस शुक्रवार थिएटर्स में रिलीज हुई फिल्म उड़ता तीर ने शानदार कमाई करते हुए पहले वीकेंड में कुल 19.45 करोड़ रुपये का आंकड़ा पार कर लिया है 📈

Sacnilk की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक फिल्म ने पहले दिन 4.10 करोड़ रुपये कमाए, शनिवार को 7.25 करोड़ रुपये का कलेक्शन किया और रविवार को 8.10 करोड़ रुपये बटोरे 💵

ट्रेड एनालिस्ट Taran Adarsh का दावा है कि शनिवार को फिल्म के कलेक्शन में 76.83 प्रतिशत का जबरदस्त उछाल आया और मुंबई, बेंगलुरु, कोलकाता जैसे बड़े सेंटर्स पर मजबूत ऑक्यूपेंसी दर्ज की गई 🏙️

आकाश ए कौशिक के निर्देशन में बनी इस फिल्म में आयुष्मान खुराना ने एक पाकिस्तानी जासूस का किरदार निभाया है जो धमाके के बाद अपनी याददाश्त खो बैठता है 🕵️‍♂️

फिल्म में राहुल बोस, राम कपूर और गुलशन ग्रोवर जैसे कलाकार भी अहम भूमिकाओं में हैं 🎭

क्या आपने थिएटर्स में जाकर उड़ता तीर देख ली है? 🍿

ctx.title: Udta Teer box office collection day 3: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan film crosses  ₹19 crore in opening weekend
ctx.summary: Udta Teer box office collection day 3: The film is a spy comedy which also features Rahul Bose, Ram Kapoor, and Suhail Nayyar.
ctx.text:
Udta Teer box office collection day 3 : Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan 's quirky take on the genre of a spy film, Udta Teer, was released in theatres this Friday. Amid box office releases like Nayyi Navelli and Prahaar from last week, the film has managed to put up a steady run in its opening weekend. After a decent release day haul, the film has shown a surprising amount of growth in the next two days. Let's take a closer look.
Udta Teer leveled up above expectations and collected ₹ 4.10 crore on its opening day in theatres. It opened to decent reviews, which helped its cause and the film gradually showed growth on Saturday to collect ₹ 7.25 crore. As per the latest update on Sacnilk, Udta Teer has grown further on Sunday, and managed to collect ₹ 8.10 crore. This brings the total collection of the film to a solid ₹ 19.45 crore after three days of release.
Taran Adarsh commented on the film's box office pull and wrote on X, "springs a wonderful surprise, witnessing a solid 76.83% jump on Saturday... The major multiplexes across urban centres have been recording strong occupancies, and the trend is expected to continue on Sunday.
While the national chains doubled their business on Saturday, several centres also witnessed a significant jump, beyond #Mumbai... #Bengaluru, #Kolkata, #Jaipur, #Hyderabad, #Pune, and #Chennai reported solid footfalls.
The film now needs to sustain this momentum through the weekdays to post a respectable Week 1 total."
Udta Teer marks the directorial debut of Akash A Kaushik, who earlier worked as a writer on movies such as Housefull 4, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3. The film follows a Pakistani spy, played by Khurrana, who loses his memory after a blast and begins to believe that he is an Indian Counter-Terrorism Squad officer. His mistaken identity sets off a chain of comic and action-packed events as he becomes caught up in a cross-border espionage operation.
It also stars Rahul Bose, Ram Kapoor, Suhail Nayyar, Gulshan Grover, late Mukul Dev, Raghubir Yadav, Brijendra Kala, Supriya Pilgaonkar and Sandeep Anand in supporting roles.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’.

A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.

Santanu continues to write passionately about films and celebrity culture. He brings a relatable, as well as critically informed, lens to entertainment and culture for a wide audience.
